questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience a new culture and I have always been interested in studying and living in the UK. It was crucial for me that my host university offered interesting courses within my field.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to find the information I needed upon arrival if I just kept myself updated on all of the emails I received. I would say that if you are not reading all your emails leading up to your exchange it is easy to miss something important, so they are definitely worth reading!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was assigned a student advisor which can be reached most days of the week and can help you with anything related to your studies, life at the study destination and personal matters. If they cannot help you, they will tell you about all the services that could then instead answer your question or help you. I was therefore never left stranded, as I had a lot of people to reach out to for help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of housing options for my host institution, which was very nice, because it made it not very difficult to get university accommodation if you send in your application. Accommodations were located widely across the city, so it is possible to pick a specific location in the city that you would most like to live in.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: As I lived in an uncatered flat of 5 people, there was a kitchen that we could use for cooking. They were very nice, as they included an oven and a microwave oven.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It might be a little bit old depending on where you decide to go, but I have mostly heard good things about the university accommodation from other exchange students and I had a good experience as well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: To sign up for courses I had to send a prioritised list of the courses I was most interested in signing up for, along with my application for the university itself. I could choose up to five courses and then they try to assign you the courses you put at the top of your list, based on availability.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could email the Visiting Student Office if you had troubles with your course registration but I did not do that, so I don't have experience on that.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful in registering for the classes I wanted. I got the courses I had placed second, third and fourth on my course registration form, but the reason I didn't get the first one was because they decided to only teach it during the spring semester, while I was there during the fall semester. I was very happy with my courses and now I am very grateful that those were the courses I received.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would read the information provided about how to register for courses and look at a lot of courses, both within and outside of your study field. I found many interesting courses outside of my field. Only list the courses you would be happy to take on your prioritised list, as it could happen that you don't get the ones you most want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses I took were third or fourth year courses for the undergraduate programs and I found them to be challenging but not too challenging.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I loved the teaching style. The use very interactive styles of teaching and the courses I had all had interactive seminar sessions and discussions which was very nice. What I loved most about the teaching style is that you get a lot of feedback from your teacher for your work during the semester compared to UCPH so when I submitted my final essays and exams I had a lot of constructive feedback to work with. I do not like how little feedback we get at UCPH and we often do not get even one sentence of feedback from our teachers during the entire semester, not even for our final exams. I feel like I learned a lot more during the semester at my host institution, and actually learned about ways I needed to improve on, something that I had never gotten a comment about at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I was enrolled in Nations and Nationalism, Sociology of Emotions and Sociology of Medicine.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of these courses to future exchange students, especially Sociology of Medicine and Sociology of Emotions. They had great teachers and I learned so much about these interesting topics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not experience any negative unexpected costs during my exchange but I did travel more than I expected so I would expect to spend some money on traveling.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was less expensive than I expected because I heard of the cost of living crisis and thought everything would be very expensive but it was still quite affordable compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were so many clubs and activities offered by my host institution, it is actually quite impossible to not find something that interests you. They have a few hundred student societies so you can join anything you want. It is incredible.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the university gym, the Pole Dancing Society and the Scandinavian Society, which were all great. The gym is affordable compared to how much you get (it is huge and has everything). I started doing pole dancing at the Pole Dancing Society as I had been wanting to try it for quite a long time now and it was so much fun. The Scandinavian Society was also very fun to meet other people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend visiting students to go on some ESN trips as they allow you to travel outside of the city and see more of the country, which is very beautiful. I went on ESN trips a lot of my weekends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy, as the weather and culture is not too different from what I was used to. I also made it easier that I stayed in an English-speaking country so being a part of the culture was easier.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Definitely go meet as many people as you can the first few weeks! You will be so tired and it will be quite a lot in the beginning but you will eventually find your friends and then it becomes much easier. I was mostly friends with other exchange students that I met through ESN meet-ups, so definitely show up to those.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not really find any cultural differences especially challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved the city, it was so beautiful and the people are very nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I would tell them to try to meet as many people as they can in the first few weeks because eventually they will find their core friend group. Try as many activities as you can, the university has so much to offer and mostly quite cheap. Enjoy every single moment, the exchange goes by so fast and even though it can be hard to be away from family and home, you are only exchange once in your life so make the most of it!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Most people are actually very open and want to get to know you, so put yourself out there.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was without a doubt the friends I made. We met during welcome week and stayed so close during the entire semester, they became my family. I will forever be grateful for Edinburgh for bringing us together.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during my exchange was not having anyone I knew close to me in the unfamiliar circumstances. I have lived away from home for some years now, but it is hard to go to a new country and not have anyone there, where it is completely your responsibility to make close friends. But these challenges only make you grow so I would still recommend doing an exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
